doc.title: Bobby Militello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002

title: Sedola's lesson on projection and thinking acoustic
summary: Sedola taught projection; Militello tells students to send the sound out and think acoustic rather than rely on the microphone.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: I bet you learned to project in that situation.

Well sure. Well Sedola gave us the projection. Yeah his whole thing was — I used to go to country clubs to hear him play weddings and things like that. And you would walk into a country club, the room was three hundred, four hundred feet long and was one of those typical country club rooms. He’s at the other side of the room. I’d walk in the door and you could hear him clear as a bell on the other side of the room with 500 people milling around and doing whatever. You’d just hear his sound clear as a bell. His thing was projection. As a matter of fact when we would play in the practice room together, the other teachers — or the two of us would play together duets and really give it some — the other teachers sometimes would have to stop teaching because we would just vibrate so much that they would say they just had to stop, they just couldn’t deal with it. One of us at a time was okay but the two of us, the extra vibration, they just couldn’t deal with it. So yeah he taught the projection, which is something I’ve always said to the kids when we do clinics and that, with Dave and Maynard and everything else. Forget about that microphone. The microphone is a tool that happens later. Right now your whole purpose is to send that sound just like a public speaker looks at the exit sign in the back and that’s his focal point.

You’ve got to send your sound out there with that kind of a feeling. If you don’t there’s always this weakness, you never fit in a section, you’ll never work in a section, it doesn’t sound right. You will never blend with the lead player. You can never do this.
Yeah. Well a microphone is only going to project what you put into it and if you don’t in something good—
Yeah but you need — to have a center in what you do you need to think acoustic. You can’t think electronic. You have to think acoustic.
